sub: Named after al-humazah, “the scorner”, in ayah 1
theme: A warning to the person who belittles people and piles up wealth, thinking it will keep him forever. The surah shows his end: thrown into al-Ḥuṭamah, Allah’s crushing Fire.
story: Revealed in Makkah, among the earliest surahs. It condemns faults the Arabs of the time already knew were wrong: mocking and belittling people, and hoarding wealth.

Reports differ on who it was first about: al-Akhnas ibn Sharīq, al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah, who insulted the Prophet ﷺ behind his back and to his face, or Umayyah ibn Khalaf. Most held that it covers anyone with these traits.
People like this often seem to thrive in this world. So the surah paints their character, then their end, and the listener sees for himself that such a person deserves it.

sections.title: Woe to the mocker counting his wealth, thinking it keeps him forever
sections.meaning: Woe to everyone who keeps finding fault with people, by look, gesture or word. He gathers wealth, counts it again and again, and thinks it will make him live forever.
points: Woe to every scorner and mocker
He piles up wealth and keeps counting it
He thinks his wealth will keep him forever
sections.matters: It names two faults everyone recognises: attacking people’s dignity and loving money more than people. It also exposes the false belief underneath hoarding, that wealth can hold off death.
sections.story: Reportedly about a Makkan leader who spoke ill of the Prophet ﷺ: al-Akhnas ibn Sharīq, al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah or Umayyah ibn Khalaf. Most said it applies to anyone who behaves like them.
explained: Wayl is a word of doom and punishment. Humazah and lumazah both describe someone who keeps finding fault with people. In one view, one does it behind their back and the other to their face; in another, one uses gestures and the other words.

His only concern is collecting wealth and counting it, not spending it on good causes or on his relatives. In his ignorance he thinks it will keep him alive in this world forever. He never realises that stinginess shortens lives and goodness lengthens them.
teaches: Mocking and belittling people is a serious sin, by word or by gesture.
Wealth itself is not blamed; hoarding it and withholding its due is.
Spend on good causes and on family, don’t just count.
sections.hook: Two rhyming labels open the surah: humazah lumazah. Then three steps, one per ayah: he mocks (1), he gathers and counts (2), he thinks it makes him last (3).

sections.title: He is flung into the Crusher, a heart-reaching Fire shut over them
sections.meaning: No! He will be flung into al-Ḥuṭamah, the Crusher. It is Allah’s blazing Fire, which reaches right into the hearts. It is shut over them, held by long stretched columns, with no way out.
points: No! He will be thrown into the Crusher
What is the Crusher? Allah’s kindled Fire
Shut over them, in stretched columns
sections.matters: It answers his false hope directly. He thought his wealth would make him last; instead he is thrown into a Fire that is sealed shut. The picture is drawn so the listener feels he has earned it.
sections.story: No specific incident. It continues the warning to the mocker and hoarder of ayat 1–3.
explained: Kallā: it is not as he thinks. He will be flung into al-Ḥuṭamah, a name of Hell meaning the one that crushes and breaks whatever is thrown in. The question “what will make you know?” shows how terrible it is. It is Allah’s own Fire, always kept blazing.

Tattaliʿu ʿalā al-afʾidah: it eats through the body until it reaches the heart. Worldly fire kills a person before it reaches the heart; this Fire reaches it while he is still alive. Then it is muʾṣadah, shut over them, fixed with long columns so they can never get out.
teaches: Security built on wealth is false security.
Allah’s punishment is real and has no exit for those who earn it.
Fear losing the Hereafter more than losing money.
sections.hook: Ayah 5 asks “What will make you know…?” and ayah 6 answers. Then the Fire closes in step by step: thrown in (4), reaches the hearts (7), shut over them (8), columns (9).

groups.text: Woe to everyone who keeps finding fault with people and belittling them.
He gathers wealth, keeps counting it, and thinks it will make him live forever.
No! He will be thrown into al-Ḥuṭamah. And what will make you know what the Crusher is?
It is Allah’s kindled Fire, which reaches right into the hearts.
It is shut over them, held by long stretched columns.

1.explain: Wayl: doom and punishment. Humazah lumazah: someone who keeps finding fault with people and belittling them, behind their back and to their face, with gestures and with words.
1.why: Reports differ: al-Akhnas ibn Sharīq, al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah, who insulted the Prophet ﷺ behind his back and to his face, Umayyah ibn Khalaf, or others. Most said it is general, for anyone with these traits.

2.explain: Jamaʿa mālan wa ʿaddadah: he piles it up and counts it again and again, saving it for hard times. His only concern is wealth, not spending it on good or on relatives.

3.explain: In his ignorance he thinks his money will keep him in this world forever, so all his effort goes into growing it.

4.explain: Kallā: never, it is not as he thinks. He will be flung into al-Ḥuṭamah, a name of Hell: it crushes and breaks whatever is thrown into it.

5.explain: A question to show how terrible the Crusher is, beyond anything you can imagine.

6.explain: It is Allah’s Fire, al-mūqadah: always kept blazing, with people and stones as its fuel.

7.explain: Tattaliʿu ʿalā al-afʾidah: it passes through the body and reaches the hearts. Worldly fire kills before it reaches the heart; this one reaches it while the person is still alive.

8.explain: Muʾṣadah: closed and sealed over them. With all that heat, they are locked in and have lost all hope of getting out.

9.explain: Fī ʿamadin mumaddadah: in long, stretched columns, of iron or of fire, fixed behind the shut gates so they can never get out.
